parallel_group.prompt:
Add arc resolution to KBUtilLib so a producer can learn which KOROS research arc it is running in.

BACKGROUND, NOT AUTHORITATIVE: agent-io/prds/kind-model-analysis-explorer-v1/fullprompt.md, committed on the wip branch and probably NOT reachable from your worktree. Everything you need is in this prompt.

HARD PRECONDITION: this task imports `kbutillib.koros_arc_store`, which is built by a DIFFERENT PRD (kind-annotation-results-explorer-v1) and must already be on main. If `from kbutillib.koros_arc_store import resolve_runs_root, KorosArcStore, AnalysisRecord` raises ImportError on main, STOP and report that the precondition is unmet. Do not create koros_arc_store yourself -- creating it here is the specific collision this split exists to prevent.

WHAT TO BUILD. One new module, `src/kbutillib/arc_context.py`, exposing exactly:

    def resolve_current_arc(explicit: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, str] | None

It returns (project, arc) or None, and it NEVER guesses. Resolution order, first match wins:
  1. `explicit` -- an arc slug passed by the caller. Resolve its project by finding the arc under the runs root and reading the `project` field of its PROVENANCE.json.
  2. The `KOROS_ARC` environment variable. KIND sets this on every session it starts (king_backend/session.py). ITS VALUE IS AN ARC SLUG, NOT A PATH -- resolve the project exactly as in step 1.
  3. The current working directory, IF it lies under `resolve_runs_root()`. The runs tree is laid out as <runs_root>/<project>/arcs/<slug>/, and a project directory may ITSELF be an arc when it has a PROVENANCE.json and no arcs/ subdirectory (KIND's own p0.py handles this case, so you must too). Walk upward from cwd to find the arc directory.
  4. Otherwise return None.

If `resolve_runs_root()` raises (no runs root resolvable on this machine), `resolve_current_arc` returns None rather than propagating -- a machine with no KOROS runs tree is a normal machine, not an error.

Also expose:

    def warn_not_indexed(reason: str) -> None

which writes ONE line to stderr saying the analysis result was not indexed and why. Nothing else -- no logging config, no exception.

TESTS. Write tests covering the full precedence chain against a synthetic runs tree built in a tmp_path fixture: explicit wins over env; env wins over cwd; cwd works when inside the tree and returns None when outside; a project dir that is itself an arc resolves; an unknown explicit slug returns None; an unresolvable runs root returns None rather than raising. Use monkeypatch for KOROS_ARC and KOROS_HOME; depend on NO real path on any machine.

SCOPE. Do not modify any existing module. Do not add a CLI verb. Do not touch kbutillib/koros_arc_store.py.

ALSO IN THIS TASK -- CAC identity helper. Add to the same module:

    APP_ID = "models-and-analyses"      # canonical HYPHEN form
    def app_us() -> str: return APP_ID.replace("-", "_")

CAC invariant I4 (king/docs/CROSS_APP_COMMUNICATION.md section E) requires ONE canonical id in hyphen form, with the underscore form DERIVED MECHANICALLY for Python modules and SQL identifiers -- computed, never hand-chosen. Write a test that asserts app_us() == APP_ID.replace('-','_') rather than asserting the literal 'models_and_analyses', because a hardcoded second spelling is exactly what I4 exists to prevent.

=== BINDING SPECIFICATIONS from confront round 1 and the shared-interface agreement (committed as kind-annotation-results-explorer-v1 draft_commit 8a2d8ab). These are not advisory. ===

RECORD SHAPE. AnalysisRecord fields are: record_id, kind, created_at, producer, subject, status, trust_tier, provenance, contract_version, artifacts, payload.
  status is ok|failed|partial and describes THE JOB.
  trust_tier is verified|homology|hypothesis|opinion and describes THE EVIDENCE.
  These are different questions. A gapfilled reaction from a cleanly-completed reconstruction is status ok AND trust_tier hypothesis. Never derive one from the other.
  provenance is a dict carrying the bridge kind and its metric; REQUIRED for any tier other than verified.
  contract_version is the integer 1.

RECORD_ID ALGORITHM, exact: sha256( lower(kind) + "\0" + lower(subject) + "\0" + canonical_json(significant_params) ).hexdigest(), where canonical_json sorts keys and uses compact separators. Significant params: template (reconstruct / model_build); media (gapfill); media + objective (fba); media + fraction_of_optimum (fva); the condition list (fitness analyses). Truncate to 32 chars for DISPLAY only, never for identity. Two independent producers computing this for the same logical analysis must agree -- test that.

STORAGE IS A PER-USER LOCAL DATABASE in the pod home directory, written by KBUtilLib's KBDL client utilities -- on by default on pods, configurable elsewhere. IT IS NOT A FILE IN THE ARC DIRECTORY. Nothing in this PRD writes into the KOROS runs tree. Chris specified this on 2026-09-23 and it REPLACES an earlier per-arc .analyses/*.jsonl sidecar design; if you find sidecar wording anywhere, the database wins.
  Any earlier instruction about per-writer sharding is WITHDRAWN -- it existed only because the runs tree is Dropbox-synced, and a pod home directory is not.
  record_analysis is an UPSERT keyed on record_id. The requirement is unchanged and still tested: re-recording the same logical analysis leaves exactly ONE row, never two.

TWO-TIER SCHEMA, and this is the part to get right. SQL COLUMNS carry ONLY navigable dimensions: run, project, arc, subject, kind, producer, status, trust_tier, timestamps, counts, and precomputed summary statistics. JSON BLOBS carry gene-level and reaction-level detail, ONE BLOB PER SUBJECT. A genome-scale model is thousands of reactions and flux across conditions multiplies it, so detail as rows would blow the row budget Chris set. read_detail(record_id) -> dict is the ONLY call that opens a blob.

EVERY PRECOMPUTED SUMMARY STATISTIC CARRIES THE VERSION OF THE CODE THAT COMPUTED IT. Without it the database silently holds two populations scored differently with nothing on the row saying which.

THE WRITE SIDE MUST FAIL SOFT. Recording is ON BY DEFAULT on pods, so it is a side effect the user never asked for. A database that is locked, full, read-only or on a filesystem that has gone away degrades to a warning and lets the analysis complete. It must NEVER fail a pipeline run.

UNATTRIBUTED IS A FIRST-CLASS STATE. record_analysis accepts a null project and arc and writes to a root-level unattributed index under the same sharding rule. Do not reject or drop null-arc records.

ARC SLUGS ARE UNIQUE PER PROJECT, NOT GLOBALLY. --arc accepts PROJECT/SLUG. A bare SLUG matching arcs in more than one project must REFUSE to stamp and print a disambiguation error. Never guess.

ARTIFACT REFS: a bare absolute path, or file://, or obj://<object_id> for the KBDL object store. Nothing else.

CANONICAL MODEL IDENTITY: artifacts.model_id = "model:<ns>:<id>", ns in {kbdl, file}. kbdl ids are the KBDL object id; file ids are the absolute normalized path of the cobra JSON.

For THIS task specifically, the parts that bind you are the per-project slug uniqueness rule (your resolver must reject an ambiguous bare slug rather than pick one) and the PROJECT/SLUG accepted form.

NOTE: the store is a per-user database, NOT a file in the arc. This task still resolves (project, arc) as the ATTRIBUTION for a record; it does not write anything into the arc directory.

RUNS-ROOT RESOLUTION -- READ THIS BEFORE CALLING resolve_runs_root(). Chris, 2026-09-23: 'KOROS_HOME should be used for the path to projects.... don't assume it's Dropbox/Science/runs.' The precedence the shared layer implements is: an explicit runs-root argument, then $KOROS_HOME/runs, then $KING_KOROS_RUNS, then RAISE. Two things to get right:
  - KOROS_HOME is the WORKSPACE ROOT; the runs tree is at $KOROS_HOME/runs. It is not itself the runs directory. (koros_start.py:24-27, research_init.py:98-102, INSTALL.md:88-92.)
  - The KING override is spelled KING_KOROS_RUNS (king_backend/config.py:25). There is NO KIND_KOROS_RUNS anywhere in the stack -- the cw-kind skill claims that name and is wrong. Do not reintroduce it.
  - NO HARDCODED FALLBACK PATH. Not ~/Dropbox/Science/runs, not anything else. If nothing resolves, that is a machine with no KOROS workspace, and resolve_current_arc returns None.

=== CONFORMANCE WITH THE SHARED SCAFFOLD (review round 1) ===
The module you import is built by PRD kind-annotation-results-explorer-v1 task p0-shared-scaffold. These rules are ENFORCED THERE, not here -- do not reimplement them, and do not work around them:
  - TRUST-TIER FLOOR RULE: a record summarizing several findings carries the LEAST-TRUSTED contributing tier. Adding higher-tier findings NEVER raises it. The store exposes NO api that raises a tier.
  - A record whose trust_tier is anything other than 'verified' and whose provenance dict is empty is REJECTED AT WRITE. Populate provenance or the write fails.
  - UNKNOWN KINDS ARE STORED AND FLAGGED, never refused. Only structural validation rejects. A foreign kind is COUNTED, never silently dropped.

IF THE SHARED MODULE RESOLVES THE RUNS ROOT FROM 'KIND_KOROS_RUNS' OR FALLS BACK TO A HARDCODED ~/Dropbox/Science/runs, THAT IS A KNOWN DEFECT IN IT -- report it, do not paper over it here. The correct precedence is explicit --runs-root, then $KOROS_HOME/runs, then $KING_KOROS_RUNS, then raise. KIND_KOROS_RUNS does not exist anywhere in the stack.
parallel_group.success_criteria: src/kbutillib/arc_context.py exists and exposes resolve_current_arc, warn_not_indexed, APP_ID and app_us; the tests this task adds pass and cover all four resolution branches plus the None cases; a test asserts app_us() is derived from APP_ID rather than hardcoded; no test that passed on the base commit fails on the branch; kbutillib/koros_arc_store.py is unmodified by this branch. resolve_current_arc accepts PROJECT/SLUG, and a bare slug that matches arcs in more than one project returns an unambiguous refusal rather than a guess, asserted by test. parallel_group.prompt:
Let a KBDL job carry the KOROS project and arc it belongs to, and stamp an analysis record when it completes.

BACKGROUND, NOT AUTHORITATIVE: the PRD lives in a DIFFERENT repo (KBUtilLib, agent-io/prds/kind-model-analysis-explorer-v1/) and is not reachable from your worktree. This prompt is self-contained.

WHY THE ARC IS A PARAMETER AND NOT AN ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE -- do not 'simplify' this: KIND injects KOROS_ARC into the environment of the SESSION processes it starts. A KBDL job executes server-side, in a different process and possibly on a different machine, where that variable is absent or, worse, inherited from something unrelated. Reading it server-side would silently index jobs to the wrong arc, and a wrong arc is a lie the UI presents as fact. The client resolves the arc and passes it in.

WHAT TO BUILD.

1. Add optional `project: str | None = None` and `arc: str | None = None` fields to JobContext (src/kbdl_service/job_types/, JobContext currently carries job_id, job_type, owner, object_store, settings). They default to None and every existing construction site must keep working untouched.
2. Thread them from job submission through to the job types, so a submitting client can set them.
3. In these three job types ONLY -- model_reconstruction.py, fitness_model_analysis.py, fitness_prop.py -- when both project and arc are set, write one analysis record on completion. When either is absent, write nothing and behave exactly as today.

RECORD SHAPE. Write one row to the per-user local database (see the storage section below). Fields: record_id, kind, created_at (ISO8601 UTC), producer (tool name and version), subject, status, artifacts (dict of named references -- use object-store object ids, never inlined data), payload (dict). Kinds are exactly: kbdl.model_build for model_reconstruction (subject = genome id; payload carries template, reaction and gene counts, atp-safe flag; artifacts carries the object ref for the cobra JSON model), kbdl.fitness_analysis for fitness_model_analysis (subject = model id; payload carries the condition list; artifacts carries object refs for the v2_fitness_simulations, v2_fitness_simulation_reaction and v2_fitness_simulation_genes gaa_data tables), kbdl.fitness_prop for fitness_prop (subject = genome id; payload carries the condition list; artifacts carries the ref to the propagated fitness table). record_id must be stable across re-runs of the same logical job so a re-run replaces rather than duplicates.

RESOLVE THE RUNS ROOT FROM THE ENVIRONMENT. NEVER HARDCODE A PATH. Chris, 2026-09-23: 'KOROS_HOME should be used for the path to projects.... don't assume it's Dropbox/Science/runs.' Precedence, first match wins:
  1. an explicit runs-root argument if the caller passes one;
  2. $KOROS_HOME/runs -- NOTE THE SHAPE: KOROS_HOME is the WORKSPACE ROOT and runs live under it at $KOROS_HOME/runs. This is koros's own convention (koros/skills/koros-start/koros_start.py:24-27, research_init.py:98-102, koros/INSTALL.md:88-92).
  3. $KING_KOROS_RUNS -- KING's override (king_backend/config.py:25). NOTE THE NAME: it is KING_KOROS_RUNS. There is NO variable called KIND_KOROS_RUNS; the cw-kind skill says there is and the skill is wrong.
If none resolves, write nothing and log one line -- never fail the job. ~/Dropbox/Science/runs is one developer's local layout, not a constant, and must not appear in the code.

DO NOT add any field to ObjectMetadata in src/kbdl_service/object_store/store.py. Its docstring states that fields are deliberately withheld and tests/test_objects_skani_version.py and tests/test_objects_checkm2_version.py assert the published payload is unchanged. The arc association lives beside the arc, not in the object store.

TESTS. A job run with project and arc set writes exactly one record with the right kind; re-running writes one, not two; a job run WITHOUT them writes nothing and its result payload is unchanged from the base commit; a missing runs root writes nothing and does not fail the job; a database that cannot be written degrades to a warning and the job still completes.

SCOPE. Three job types only. No new job type. No change to the clearinghouse or the lake schema. No web app.

ALSO REQUIRED -- CAC TRUST TIERS (invariant I2, from king/docs/CROSS_APP_COMMUNICATION.md section A; you will not have that repo, so the rule is stated in full here). Every record's payload MUST carry:
  trust_tier      -- one of verified | homology | hypothesis | opinion
  provenance -- the evidence that tier requires

ASSIGNMENT IS FIXED, not per-run judgement:
  kbdl.model_build      -> hypothesis. Model-generated, argued not proven. provenance: template + the arc + the reconstruction's provenance.
  kbdl.fitness_analysis -> hypothesis. provenance: conditions + the model record it derives from.
  kbdl.fitness_prop     -> homology, NOT hypothesis. This is the one that is easy to get wrong. Propagation reaches a gene through a PROTEIN HOMOLOG, and the CAC reserves `homology` for exactly that -- evidence via a sequence or structure homolog. It REQUIRES the bridge metric and the accession reached through, so provenance MUST carry the percent identity of the hit and the reference accession. kbdl-fitness-prop-v1's whole design rationale is that search-based propagation yields percent identity per hit where clustering could not, so the value exists in that job's result; find its actual field name in the source rather than assuming one, and if it genuinely is not available, record provenance with an explicit null for the metric and say so in the task report -- do NOT silently downgrade to hypothesis or fabricate a metric.

Without the tier on the record, propagated fitness and measured fitness render identically, which the contract names as the category error.

Test that each of the three job types writes its specified tier and a non-empty provenance, and specifically that fitness_prop writes 'homology' and not 'hypothesis'.

{

  "id": "models-and-analyses",
  "title": "Models and Analyses",
  "description": "Metabolic models and their analyses across your projects and arcs.",
  "contract_version": 1,

{port} and {proxy_path} are filled by KIND's launcher -- leave them literal.

Installing this app would then silently remove unrelated capabilities from the user's KIND, an effect with no visible connection to its cause. SCOPE. No changes to any of the five KIND repos. No new endpoints.

ID DISCIPLINE (CAC I4): the manifest `id`, the manifest BASENAME, the console command and the distribution name are ONE string. Take it from kbutillib.arc_context.APP_ID; do not write the literal in more than one place. A test should assert the written manifest's id equals APP_ID and that the filename is APP_ID + '.json'.

contract_version is REQUIRED in the manifest from v1 (CAC section F) -- a manifest without it is malformed for its declared version.

=== BINDING SPECIFICATIONS from confront round 1 ===

MANIFEST INSTALL PATH, exact: $KING_STATE/kind-apps/plugins when KING_STATE is set, otherwise $HOME/kind-apps/plugins. Then refresh the union symlink farm. Never king/plugins/. Do not hardcode $HOME -- KING_STATE differs on the pod.

BACKFILL SCAN, exact: walk <runs_root>/*/arcs/*/ for *.model.json, fba/*.json, fva/*.json. Where the KBDL object store is reachable, ADDITIONALLY list by object_type in {model, fba, fva} filtered by owner. PREFER FILE ARTIFACTS; use store refs only where no file is present. Records it cannot attribute to an arc go to the unattributed index, not to /dev/null.



BACKFILL EMITS A COVERAGE REPORT, not a success count: arcs scanned, records written, AND an explicit list of artifacts found-but-unattributable and analyses referenced-but-missing. Without that list an operator sees a successful run over a partial index and cannot tell the difference. Records it cannot attribute go to the unattributed index; records whose artifacts are gone are listed as missing, not silently skipped.
parallel_group.success_criteria: the app self-registers its manifest on `serve` and skips registration under --no-king; kbu kind install also writes it; the manifest is written to ~/kind-apps/plugins/models-and-analyses.json as a real file carrying contract_version 1, and a test asserts king/plugins/ is untouched; a test asserts the manifest id and basename both derive from kbutillib.arc_context.APP_ID rather than a repeated literal; the symlink farm links upstream manifests non-clobberingly and skips .disabled entries; both the ~/king-stack and flat-$HOME KING_ROOT layouts resolve in tests; kbu arc backfill is idempotent across two runs, honours --dry-run, and marks every record payload.provenance=inferred; the tests this task adds pass and no test that passed on the base commit fails on the branch. The manifest path honours KING_STATE with a documented $HOME fallback; backfill prefers file artifacts over store refs, routes unattributable records to the unattributed index, and  backfill emits a coverage report listing unattributable artifacts and missing analyses rather than only a written-count.
